   280→## Noise Functions
   281→
   282→```vex
   283→// ── Perlin noise (0..1 output, smooth) ────────────────────────────────────
   284→float  n1  = noise(@P);                             // position-based, 0..1
   285→float  n2  = noise(@P * 3.0);                       // 3× frequency
   286→float  n3  = noise(@P + @Time * 0.5);               // animated (no sliding)
   287→vector vn  = noise(@P);                             // vector noise (3 channels)
   288→
   289→// ── Signed Perlin (-1..1) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   290→float  sn  = snoise(@P);                            // -1..1
   291→
   292→// ── Fractal Brownian Motion (layered octaves) ─────────────────────────────
   293→float fbm  = 0;
   294→float amp  = 0.5;
   295→vector pos = @P;
   296→for(int oct = 0; oct < 5; oct++) {
   297→    fbm += snoise(pos) * amp;
   298→    pos *= 2.1;                                     // frequency doubles each octave
   299→    amp *= 0.5;                                     // amplitude halves (persistence)
   300→}
   301→@P.y += fbm * ch("height");
   302→
   303→// ── Curl noise (divergence-free, mass-conserving) ─────────────────────────
   304→// Ideal for smoke advection, flow fields — does not pile up or drain
   305→vector curl = curlnoise(@P * ch("freq") + @Time * 0.2);
   306→@v += curl * ch("strength");                        // add turbulence to velocity
   307→
   308→// ── Alligator noise (cellular, sharp creases) ─────────────────────────────
   309→float  an  = anoise(@P * 2.0);                      // 0..1, cellular look
   310→
   311→// ── Voronoi noise (cell distance + cell ID) ───────────────────────────────
   312→vector cellP;
   313→float  F1, F2;
   314→int    cellID;
   315→wnoise(@P, 0, F1, F2, cellP, cellID);              // F1=nearest-cell-dist, F2=second-nearest
   316→float  edge = F2 - F1;                              // Worley edge factor
   317→
   318→// ── Flow noise (animated without temporal sliding) ────────────────────────
   319→float  fn  = flownoise(@P, @Time * 0.3);            // 4th arg is flow parameter
   320→
   321→// ── Simplex noise (faster, fewer directional artifacts than Perlin) ────────
   322→float  xn  = xnoise(@P);                            // -1..1 range
   323→
   324→// ── Classic Houdini noise (original implementation) ───────────────────────
   325→float  on  = onoise(@P);                            // 0..1

   385→## Matrix and Quaternion Functions
   386→
   387→```vex
   388→// ── Build transform matrices ──────────────────────────────────────────────
   389→matrix4 ident4 = ident();                           // 4×4 identity
   390→matrix3 ident3 = ident3();                          // 3×3 identity
   391→
   392→// maketransform: order (e.g. XFORM_SRT), translate, rotate (radians), scale
   393→matrix4 xf  = maketransform(XFORM_SRT,
   394→                             {0,1,0},               // translate
   395→                             {0, radians(45), 0},   // rotate Y 45°
   396→                             {2, 2, 2});             // uniform scale 2×
   397→
   398→// ── Decompose / invert ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   399→matrix4 inv = invert(xf);                           // inverse transform
   400→matrix4 tp  = transpose(xf);                        // transpose (useful for normals)
   401→float   det = determinant(xf);                      // scalar determinant
   402→
   403→// ── Transform points and vectors ─────────────────────────────────────────
   404→vector  tp2 = @P * xf;                              // transform point (homogeneous)
   405→vector  tv  = vtransform(xf, @v);                   // transform direction (no translate)
   406→vector  tn  = ntransform(xf, @N);                   // transform normal (uses inverse-transpose)
   407→
   408→// ── Look-at orientation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
   409→vector  eye  = @P;
   410→vector  tgt  = {0, 0, 0};
   411→vector  upv  = {0, 1, 0};
   412→matrix3 lookR = lookat(eye, tgt, upv);              // rotation matrix facing target
   413→
   414→// ── Quaternion construction and use ──────────────────────────────────────
   415→vector4 q1  = quaternion(radians(90), {0,1,0});     // 90° around Y axis
   416→vector4 q2  = quaternion(matrix3(lookR));           // from rotation matrix
   417→vector4 q3  = slerp(q1, q2, 0.5);                  // blend two quaternions
   418→
   419→vector  rotV = qrotate(q1, {1,0,0});                // rotate vector by quaternion
   420→matrix3 qMat = qconvert(q1);                        // quaternion → matrix3
   421→
   422→// ── dihedral: minimal rotation from one vector to another ────────────────
   423→// Used to align copy-to-points orientation
   424→vector4 dq  = dihedral({0,0,1}, @N);               // rotation from +Z to @N
   425→@orient = dq;                                       // assign to orient for copy-stamp
   426→
   427→// ── Euler ↔ quaternion ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   428→vector  euler = {0, radians(45), 0};                // YXZ Euler in radians
   429→vector4 qe   = eulertoquaternion(euler, XFORM_XYZ);
   430→vector  back = quaterniontoeuler(qe, XFORM_XYZ);

   492→float freq = ch("frequency");

   507→int   handle = pcopen(0, "P", @P, ch("radius"), chi("maxpts"));
   508→@P = pcfilter(handle, "P");
   509→pcclose(handle);
   510→
   511→// ── Stable random color per piece (survives reorder) ─────────────────────
   512→// Run Over: Points (requires i@id attribute)
   513→float seed = i@id * 1234567.0;
   514→v@Cd = set(rand(seed), rand(seed + 1), rand(seed + 2));
   515→
   516→// ── Velocity from position delta (two-input wrangle) ─────────────────────
   517→// Input 0 = current frame, Input 1 = previous frame geo (Time Shift SOP)
   518→// Run Over: Points
   519→vector prev = point(1, "P", @ptnum);
   520→@v = (@P - prev) / @TimeInc;
   521→
   522→// ── Ray-project to surface ────────────────────────────────────────────────
   523→// Input 0 = points to project, Input 1 = target surface
   524→// Run Over: Points
   525→vector hitP, hitUV;
   526→float  d = intersect(1, @P + {0,5,0}, {0,-1,0}, hitP, hitUV);
   527→if (d >= 0) @P.y = hitP.y;
   528→
   529→// ── Closest-surface normal transfer ──────────────────────────────────────
   530→// Run Over: Points
   531→int    nearPrim;
   532→vector nearUV;
   533→xyzdist(1, @P, nearPrim, nearUV);
   534→@N = primuv(1, "N", nearPrim, nearUV);
   535→
   536→// ── Build a procedural grid (detail wrangle) ──────────────────────────────
   537→// Run Over: Detail
   538→int   cols = chi("cols");
   539→int   rows = chi("rows");
   540→float spacing = ch("spacing");
   541→for(int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
   542→    for(int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
   543→        vector pos = set(c * spacing, 0, r * spacing);
   544→        int    pt  = addpoint(0, pos);
   545→        setpointattrib(0, "Cd", pt, set(rand(pt), rand(pt+1), rand(pt+2)), "set");
   546→    }
   547→}
   548→
   549→// ── FBM noise macro (reusable via #define or inline) ─────────────────────
   550→// Run Over: Points
   551→float fbm_noise(vector p; int octaves; float persistence; float lacunarity) {
   552→    float result = 0;
   553→    float amp    = 0.5;
   554→    vector pos   = p;
   555→    for(int i = 0; i < octaves; i++) {
   556→        result += snoise(pos) * amp;
   557→        pos    *= lacunarity;
   558→        amp    *= persistence;
   559→    }
   560→    return result;
   561→}
   562→@P.y += fbm_noise(@P, 6, 0.5, 2.0) * ch("height");
   563→
   564→// ── Matrix transform: rotate a vector about arbitrary axis ────────────────
   565→// Run Over: Points
   566→float   angle  = ch("angle_deg");
   567→vector  axis   = normalize(chv("axis"));
   568→vector4 q      = quaternion(radians(angle), axis);
   569→@P             = qrotate(q, @P) + chv("pivot_offset");
   570→
   571→// ── String attribute from ptnum with padding ──────────────────────────────
   572→// Run Over: Points
   573→s@name = sprintf("geo_%04d", @ptnum);
   574→
   575→// ── Wrangle function: signed distance to plane ────────────────────────────
   576→// Run Over: Points
   577→float sdf_plane(vector p; vector origin; vector normal) {
   578→    return dot(p - origin, normalize(normal));
   579→}
   580→float dist = sdf_plane(@P, chv("plane_origin"), chv("plane_normal"));
   581→@Cd = dist > 0 ? {0,1,0} : {1,0,0};   // green above, red below
   582→```

# PXR Plugin Path & Discovery Reference

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Separator |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` | Directories containing USD plugins | `;` (Windows), `:` (Linux/Mac) |
| `PXR_AR_DEFAULT_SEARCH_PATH` | Asset resolver search paths | `;` / `:` |
| `HOUDINI_PATH` | Houdini resource paths (includes `dso/` scanning) | `;` / `:` |

**Primary:** `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` is the main mechanism for USD plugin discovery in Houdini.

## Discovery Mechanism

### How PlugRegistry Finds Plugins

```
1. Scan each directory in PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME
2. Look for plugInfo.json in that directory
3. If plugInfo.json has "Includes", follow those patterns
4. Parse each discovered plugInfo.json
5. Register Types based on "bases" declarations
6. Load libraries on demand (lazy loading)
```

### The Includes Directive

A `plugInfo.json` can reference subdirectories:

```json
{
    "Includes": ["*/resources/"]
}
```

This tells PlugRegistry: "scan every immediate subdirectory's `resources/` folder for more `plugInfo.json` files."

**Pattern matching:**
| Pattern | Matches |
|---------|---------|
| `*/resources/` | `hdFoo/resources/`, `usdBar/resources/` |
| `*/` | Every immediate subdirectory |
| `subdir/` | Specific subdirectory only |

**Recursive:** Includes are NOT recursive by default. `*/resources/` scans one level of subdirectories, not deeper.

### Discovery Example (hdCarWash)

```
PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME = C:/Users/User/houdini21.0/dso/usd

    63→
    64→**Result:** PlugRegistry discovers both `hdCarWash` (delegate DLL) and `usdCarWash` (schema) from a single `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` entry.
    65→
    66→### Houdini's Built-in Plugin Paths
    67→
    68→Houdini automatically adds these to the plugin search (no manual config needed):
    69→
    70→```
    71→$HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/          <- Karma, Storm, etc.
    72→$HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/*/resources/
    73→$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/dso/usd/        <- User plugins (if exists)
    74→```

    77→- `$HFS` = Houdini install dir (e.g., `C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 21.0.512`)
    78→- `$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR` = User prefs (e.g., `C:\Users\User\houdini21.0`)
    79→
    80→## Houdini Package System
    81→
    82→### Package Files
    83→
    84→JSON files in `packages/` directories that set environment variables before Houdini starts.
    85→
    86→**Search locations (in order):**
    87→```
    88→$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/packages/        <- C:\Users\User\houdini21.0\packages\
    89→$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/../packages/     <- C:\Users\User\Documents\houdini21.0\packages\
    90→$HFS/packages/                          <- System-wide (rare)
    91→```
    92→
    93→### Package Format
    94→
    95→```json
    96→{
    97→    "env": [
    98→        {
    99→            "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
   100→                "value": "C:/path/to/plugins",
   101→                "method": "append"
   102→            }
   103→        }
   104→    ]
   105→}
   106→```
   107→
   108→| Field | Values | Purpose |
   109→|-------|--------|---------|
   110→| `method` | `"append"` | Add to end of existing path |
   111→| `method` | `"prepend"` | Add to beginning (higher priority) |
   112→| `method` | `"set"` | Replace entirely (dangerous) |
   113→
   114→### Multiple Variables in One Package
   115→
   116→```json
   117→{
   118→    "env": [
   119→        {
   120→            "HOUDINI_PATH": {
   121→                "value": "C:/my/plugin",
   122→                "method": "prepend"
   123→            }
   124→        },
   125→        {
   126→            "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
   127→                "value": "C:/my/plugin",
   128→                "method": "prepend"
   129→            }
   130→        }
   131→    ],
   132→    "path": "C:/my/plugin"
   133→}
   134→```
   135→
   136→The `"path"` key at root level adds to `HOUDINI_PATH` directly (shorthand).
   137→
   138→## Dual-Location Deployment Pattern
   139→
   140→### Why Two Locations
   141→
   142→| Location | Purpose | When Loaded |
   143→|----------|---------|-------------|
   144→| **Source (project dir)** | Development, git tracking | Via `Documents/houdini21.0/packages/` |
   145→| **Runtime (dso/usd/)** | Production, Houdini auto-discovery | Via `houdini21.0/packages/` or auto |
   146→
   147→### Example: hdCarWash Dual Deployment
   148→
   149→**Location 1: Source (git-tracked)**
   150→```
   151→C:\Users\User\Downloads\HDCARWAASH\HdCarWash\plugin\
   152→+-- plugInfo.json                   <- Includes + delegate
   153→+-- lib\hdCarWash.dll
   154→+-- usdCarWash\resources\
   155→    +-- generatedSchema.usda
   156→    +-- plugInfo.json
   157→```
   158→
   159→Package: `Documents\houdini21.0\packages\hdCarWash.json`
   160→```json
   161→{
   162→    "env": [
   163→        {"HOUDINI_PATH": {"value": "C:/Users/.../plugin", "method": "prepend"}},
   164→        {"PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {"value": "C:/Users/.../plugin", "method": "prepend"}}
   165→    ]
   166→}
   167→```
   168→
   169→**Location 2: Runtime (user prefs)**
   170→```
   171→C:\Users\User\houdini21.0\dso\usd\
   172→+-- plugInfo.json                   <- Includes
   173→+-- hdCarWash\resources\...
   174→+-- usdCarWash\resources\...
   175→```
   176→
   177→Package: `houdini21.0\packages\hdCarWash.json`
   178→```json
   179→{
   180→    "env": [{
   181→        "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
   182→            "value": "C:/Users/User/houdini21.0/dso/usd",
   183→            "method": "append"
   184→        }
   185→    }]

   188→
   189→**Important:** If both packages exist, both paths are added. Houdini uses the first plugin it finds with a given name. Use `prepend` for the location you want to take priority.
   190→
   191→## Verifying Discovery (hython)
   192→
   193→```python
   194→# Check what plugins are registered
   195→from pxr import Plug
   196→reg = Plug.Registry()
   197→all_plugins = reg.GetAllPlugins()
   198→print(f"Total plugins: {len(all_plugins)}")
   199→
   200→# Find specific plugin
   201→for p in all_plugins:
   202→    if "CarWash" in p.name or "Karma" in p.name:
   203→        print(f"  {p.name}: {p.path}")
   204→
   205→# Check if schema is registered
   206→from pxr import Usd
   207→defn = Usd.SchemaRegistry().FindAppliedAPIPrimDefinition("MyRenderSettingsAPI")
   208→if defn:
   209→    print("Schema registered!")
   210→    for prop in defn.GetPropertyNames():
   211→        print(f"  {prop}")
   212→else:
   213→    print("Schema NOT found")
   214→
   215→# Check environment
   216→import os
   217→print("PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME:", os.environ.get("PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME", "NOT SET"))
   218→```
   219→
   220→### hython Quick Verification Script
   221→
   222→```bash
   223→# Windows (from Houdini bin/)
   224→hython -c "from pxr import Plug; [print(p.name) for p in Plug.Registry().GetAllPlugins() if 'CarWash' in p.name]"
   225→```
   226→
   227→## plugInfo.json Root and Path Resolution
   228→
   229→### Root Field
   230→
   231→The `Root` field in `plugInfo.json` sets the base directory for resolving `LibraryPath` and `ResourcePath`:
   232→
   233→```json
   234→{
   235→    "Root": ".",
   236→    "LibraryPath": "lib/hdCarWash.dll",
   237→    "ResourcePath": "resources"
   238→}
   239→```
   240→
   241→| Root | Resolves Relative To |
   242→|------|---------------------|
   243→| `"."` | Directory containing this `plugInfo.json` |
   244→| `".."` | Parent of directory containing `plugInfo.json` |
   245→| Absolute path | Fixed location (avoid -- not portable) |
   246→
   247→### Common Layouts and Their Root Values
   248→
   249→**Flat layout** (plugInfo.json next to lib/):
   250→```
   251→plugin/
   252→+-- plugInfo.json           <- Root: "."
   253→+-- lib/hdFoo.dll           <- LibraryPath: "lib/hdFoo.dll"
   254→+-- resources/
   255→    +-- generatedSchema.usda
   256→```
   257→
   258→**Nested layout** (plugInfo.json inside resources/):
   259→```
   260→usdFoo/
   261→+-- resources/
   262→|   +-- plugInfo.json       <- Root: ".."
   263→|   +-- generatedSchema.usda
   264→+-- lib/
   265→    +-- usdFoo.dll          <- LibraryPath: "lib/usdFoo.dll" (relative to Root="..")
   266→```
   267→
   268→## Common Issues
   269→
   270→| Issue | Cause | Fix |
   271→|-------|-------|-----|
   272→| Plugin not discovered | PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME missing or wrong | Check `hython -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME'))"` |
   273→| Schema found but delegate missing | Path points to schema dir only | Point to parent with Includes, not individual resource dir |
   274→| Package not loading | Wrong packages/ directory | Use `houdini21.0/packages/` (not `houdini21.0.512/packages/`) |
   275→| DLL not found despite correct path | Root field wrong | Check Root + LibraryPath concatenation resolves correctly |
   276→| Duplicate plugin warnings | Same plugin on path twice | Remove one of the dual deployment locations |
   277→| `method: set` overrides everything | Replaces entire path variable | Use `append` or `prepend` instead |
   278→
   279→## Path Priority (Highest First)
   280→
   281→```
   282→1. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (prepend entries)     <- User overrides
   283→2. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (append entries)      <- Additional plugins
   284→3. $HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/            <- Houdini built-in (Karma, Storm)
   285→4. $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/dso/usd/          <- User prefs auto-scan
   286→```
   287→
   288→Within each path, the first-discovered plugin with a given name wins.
   289→
   290→---

## plugInfo.json Root and Path Resolution

### Root Field

The `Root` field in `plugInfo.json` sets the base directory for resolving `LibraryPath` and `ResourcePath`:

```json
{
    "Root": ".",
    "LibraryPath": "lib/hdCarWash.dll",
    "ResourcePath": "resources"
}
```

| Root | Resolves Relative To |
|------|---------------------|
| `"."` | Directory containing this `plugInfo.json` |
| `".."` | Parent of directory containing `plugInfo.json` |
| Absolute path | Fixed location (avoid -- not portable) |

### Common Layouts and Their Root Values

**Flat layout** (plugInfo.json next to lib/):
```
plugin/
+-- plugInfo.json           <- Root: "."
+-- lib/hdFoo.dll           <- LibraryPath: "lib/hdFoo.dll"
+-- resources/
    +-- generatedSchema.usda
```

**Nested layout** (plugInfo.json inside resources/):
```
usdFoo/
+-- resources/
|   +-- plugInfo.json       <- Root: ".."
|   +-- generatedSchema.usda
+-- lib/
    +-- usdFoo.dll          <- LibraryPath: "lib/usdFoo.dll" (relative to Root="..")
```

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Plugin not discovered | PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME missing or wrong | Check `hython -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME'))"` |
| Schema found but delegate missing | Path points to schema dir only | Point to parent with Includes, not individual resource dir |
| Package not loading | Wrong packages/ directory | Use `houdini21.0/packages/` (not `houdini21.0.512/packages/`) |
| DLL not found despite correct path | Root field wrong | Check Root + LibraryPath concatenation resolves correctly |
| Duplicate plugin warnings | Same plugin on path twice | Remove one of the dual deployment locations |
| `method: set` overrides everything | Replaces entire path variable | Use `append` or `prepend` instead |

## Path Priority (Highest First)

```
1. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (prepend entries)     <- User overrides
2. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (append entries)      <- Additional plugins
3. $HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/            <- Houdini built-in (Karma, Storm)
4. $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/dso/usd/          <- User prefs auto-scan
```

Within each path, the first-discovered plugin with a given name wins.

# Create a Houdini package file for a USD plugin
import json
import os

def create_houdini_package(plugin_name, plugin_path,
                           packages_dir=None, method="prepend"):
    """Create a package JSON file for USD plugin discovery.
    method: 'prepend' (high priority), 'append' (low priority), 'set' (replace)."""
    if packages_dir is None:
        packages_dir = os.path.expandvars(
            "$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/packages")

    package = {
        "env": [
            {
                "HOUDINI_PATH": {
                    "value": plugin_path.replace("\\", "/"),
                    "method": method,
                }
            },
            {
                "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
                    "value": plugin_path.replace("\\", "/"),
                    "method": method,
                }
            },
        ],
        "path": plugin_path.replace("\\", "/"),
    }

    os.makedirs(packages_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = os.path.join(packages_dir, f"{plugin_name}.json")
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(package, f, indent=4, sort_keys=True)
    print(f"Package written: {out_path}")
    return out_path

# PXR Plugin Path & Discovery Reference

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Purpose | Separator |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` | Directories containing USD plugins | `;` (Windows), `:` (Linux/Mac) |
| `PXR_AR_DEFAULT_SEARCH_PATH` | Asset resolver search paths | `;` / `:` |
| `HOUDINI_PATH` | Houdini resource paths (includes `dso/` scanning) | `;` / `:` |

**Primary:** `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` is the main mechanism for USD plugin discovery in Houdini.

## Discovery Mechanism

### How PlugRegistry Finds Plugins

```
1. Scan each directory in PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME
2. Look for plugInfo.json in that directory
3. If plugInfo.json has "Includes", follow those patterns
4. Parse each discovered plugInfo.json
5. Register Types based on "bases" declarations
6. Load libraries on demand (lazy loading)
```

### The Includes Directive

A `plugInfo.json` can reference subdirectories:

```json
{
    "Includes": ["*/resources/"]
}
```

This tells PlugRegistry: "scan every immediate subdirectory's `resources/` folder for more `plugInfo.json` files."

**Pattern matching:**
| Pattern | Matches |
|---------|---------|
| `*/resources/` | `hdFoo/resources/`, `usdBar/resources/` |
| `*/` | Every immediate subdirectory |
| `subdir/` | Specific subdirectory only |

**Recursive:** Includes are NOT recursive by default. `*/resources/` scans one level of subdirectories, not deeper.

### Discovery Example (hdCarWash)

```
PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME = C:/Users/User/houdini21.0/dso/usd

dso/usd/
+-- plugInfo.json                       <- {"Includes": ["*/resources/"]}
+-- hdCarWash/
|   +-- lib/hdCarWash.dll
|   +-- resources/
|       +-- plugInfo.json               <- Delegate (Type: library)
+-- usdCarWash/
    +-- resources/
        +-- generatedSchema.usda        <- Schema definition
        +-- plugInfo.json               <- Schema (Type: resource)
```

**Result:** PlugRegistry discovers both `hdCarWash` (delegate DLL) and `usdCarWash` (schema) from a single `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME` entry.

### Houdini's Built-in Plugin Paths

Houdini automatically adds these to the plugin search (no manual config needed):

```
$HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/          <- Karma, Storm, etc.
$HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/*/resources/
$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/dso/usd/        <- User plugins (if exists)
```

Where:
- `$HFS` = Houdini install dir (e.g., `C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 21.0.512`)
- `$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR` = User prefs (e.g., `C:\Users\User\houdini21.0`)

## Houdini Package System

### Package Files

JSON files in `packages/` directories that set environment variables before Houdini starts.

**Search locations (in order):**
```
$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/packages/        <- C:\Users\User\houdini21.0\packages\
$HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/../packages/     <- C:\Users\User\Documents\houdini21.0\packages\
$HFS/packages/                          <- System-wide (rare)
```

### Package Format

```json
{
    "env": [
        {
            "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
                "value": "C:/path/to/plugins",
                "method": "append"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

| Field | Values | Purpose |
|-------|--------|---------|
| `method` | `"append"` | Add to end of existing path |
| `method` | `"prepend"` | Add to beginning (higher priority) |
| `method` | `"set"` | Replace entirely (dangerous) |

### Multiple Variables in One Package

```json
{
    "env": [
        {
            "HOUDINI_PATH": {
                "value": "C:/my/plugin",
                "method": "prepend"
            }
        },
        {
            "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
                "value": "C:/my/plugin",
                "method": "prepend"
            }
        }
    ],
    "path": "C:/my/plugin"
}
```

The `"path"` key at root level adds to `HOUDINI_PATH` directly (shorthand).

## Dual-Location Deployment Pattern

### Why Two Locations

| Location | Purpose | When Loaded |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| **Source (project dir)** | Development, git tracking | Via `Documents/houdini21.0/packages/` |
| **Runtime (dso/usd/)** | Production, Houdini auto-discovery | Via `houdini21.0/packages/` or auto |

### Example: hdCarWash Dual Deployment

**Location 1: Source (git-tracked)**
```
C:\Users\User\Downloads\HDCARWAASH\HdCarWash\plugin\
+-- plugInfo.json                   <- Includes + delegate
+-- lib\hdCarWash.dll
+-- usdCarWash\resources\
    +-- generatedSchema.usda
    +-- plugInfo.json
```

Package: `Documents\houdini21.0\packages\hdCarWash.json`
```json
{
    "env": [
        {"HOUDINI_PATH": {"value": "C:/Users/.../plugin", "method": "prepend"}},
        {"PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {"value": "C:/Users/.../plugin", "method": "prepend"}}
    ]
}
```

**Location 2: Runtime (user prefs)**
```
C:\Users\User\houdini21.0\dso\usd\
+-- plugInfo.json                   <- Includes
+-- hdCarWash\resources\...
+-- usdCarWash\resources\...
```

Package: `houdini21.0\packages\hdCarWash.json`
```json
{
    "env": [{
        "PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME": {
            "value": "C:/Users/User/houdini21.0/dso/usd",
            "method": "append"
        }
    }]
}
```

**Important:** If both packages exist, both paths are added. Houdini uses the first plugin it finds with a given name. Use `prepend` for the location you want to take priority.

# Check environment

hython -c "from pxr import Plug; [print(p.name) for p in Plug.Registry().GetAllPlugins() if 'CarWash' in p.name]"
```

## plugInfo.json Root and Path Resolution

### Root Field

The `Root` field in `plugInfo.json` sets the base directory for resolving `LibraryPath` and `ResourcePath`:

```json
{
    "Root": ".",
    "LibraryPath": "lib/hdCarWash.dll",
    "ResourcePath": "resources"
}
```

| Root | Resolves Relative To |
|------|---------------------|
| `"."` | Directory containing this `plugInfo.json` |
| `".."` | Parent of directory containing `plugInfo.json` |
| Absolute path | Fixed location (avoid -- not portable) |

### Common Layouts and Their Root Values

**Flat layout** (plugInfo.json next to lib/):
```
plugin/
+-- plugInfo.json           <- Root: "."
+-- lib/hdFoo.dll           <- LibraryPath: "lib/hdFoo.dll"
+-- resources/
    +-- generatedSchema.usda
```

**Nested layout** (plugInfo.json inside resources/):
```
usdFoo/
+-- resources/
|   +-- plugInfo.json       <- Root: ".."
|   +-- generatedSchema.usda
+-- lib/
    +-- usdFoo.dll          <- LibraryPath: "lib/usdFoo.dll" (relative to Root="..")
```

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Plugin not discovered | PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME missing or wrong | Check `hython -c "import os; print(os.environ.get('PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME'))"` |
| Schema found but delegate missing | Path points to schema dir only | Point to parent with Includes, not individual resource dir |
| Package not loading | Wrong packages/ directory | Use `houdini21.0/packages/` (not `houdini21.0.512/packages/`) |
| DLL not found despite correct path | Root field wrong | Check Root + LibraryPath concatenation resolves correctly |
| Duplicate plugin warnings | Same plugin on path twice | Remove one of the dual deployment locations |
| `method: set` overrides everything | Replaces entire path variable | Use `append` or `prepend` instead |

## Path Priority (Highest First)

```
1. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (prepend entries)     <- User overrides
2. PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME (append entries)      <- Additional plugins
3. $HFS/houdini/dso/usd_plugins/            <- Houdini built-in (Karma, Storm)
4. $HOUDINI_USER_PREF_DIR/dso/usd/          <- User prefs auto-scan
```

Within each path, the first-discovered plugin with a given name wins.

# USD Stage Composition and Layer Workflows

## Composition Arcs (LIVRPS)

USD resolves opinions via **LIVRPS** strength ordering (strongest first):

| Arc | Strength | Use Case | Example |
|-----|----------|----------|---------|
| **L**ocal opinions | 1 (strongest) | Direct attribute edits on a prim | `prim.GetAttribute("radius").Set(2.0)` |
| **I**nherits | 2 | Share properties across prim classes | `inherits = </class/hero>` |
| **V**ariantSets | 3 | Switchable options on a prim | `variantSet "color" = { "red" { ... } "blue" { ... } }` |
| **R**eferences | 4 | Bring in external assets | `references = @./assets/chair.usd@` |
| **P**ayloads | 5 | Deferred-load references (lazy) | `payload = @./heavy_geo.usd@` |
| **S**ublayers | 6 (weakest) | Stack layers in a stage | `subLayers = [@./anim.usd@, @./model.usd@]` |

**Key rule**: A stronger arc's opinion always wins. Local edits override everything.

## Layer Stacking Patterns

### Multi-Department Pipeline

Standard production layer order (top = strongest):

```
shot_final.usd          (sublayer - comp's final tweaks)
  shot_fx.usd           (sublayer - FX overrides)
    shot_lighting.usd   (sublayer - lighting department)
      shot_anim.usd     (sublayer - animation curves)
        shot_layout.usd (sublayer - layout positions)
          asset.usd     (reference - model/materials)
```

Each department only edits their layer. Opinions cascade: lighting can override layout positions, FX can override lighting visibility.

### In Houdini/Solaris

```
sublayer1 (LOP) -> sublayer2 (LOP) -> merge (LOP)
```

- **Sublayer**: Stacks opinions (weaker than existing). Use for department overrides.
- **Reference**: Brings in an asset under a prim path. Use for asset loading.
- **Graft**: Moves a prim subtree to a new location. Use for scene assembly.

### Reference vs Sublayer Decision

| Scenario | Use | Why |
|----------|-----|-----|
| Loading an asset (chair, tree, character) | Reference | Isolates asset under target prim, can instance |
| Adding department overrides (lighting, FX) | Sublayer | Stacks on existing stage, opinions merge |

```
/World

### Naming Conventions

- Use **snake_case** for prim names (not camelCase)
- Group by function: `/cameras/`, `/lights/`, `/geo/`, `/materials/`
- Assets get their own scope: `/geo/hero/` not `/hero/`
- Materials live under `/materials/` or `/World/materials/`

## Common Prim Types

| Type | Category | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `Xform` | Transform | Grouping node with transform |
| `Mesh` | Geometry | Polygonal mesh |
| `BasisCurves` | Geometry | Curves (hair, wires) |

| `DiskLight` | Lighting | Area light (disk) |
| `SphereLight` | Lighting | Point/sphere light |

USD uses an ordered stack of transform operations:

```
xformOp:translate    -> position
xformOp:rotateXYZ   -> rotation (Euler)
xformOp:scale        -> scale
```

The `xformOpOrder` attribute defines execution order (right-to-left):
```python
xformOpOrder = ["xformOp:translate", "xformOp:rotateXYZ", "xformOp:scale"]
# Applied as: Scale first, then Rotate, then Translate
```

### Common Transform Operations

```python
# Houdini Python (inside LOP context)
from pxr import UsdGeom, Gf

stage = hou.pwd().editableStage()
prim = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/geo/hero")
xform = UsdGeom.Xformable(prim)

# Set translate
xform.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(1.0, 2.0, 3.0))

# Set rotation (degrees)
xform.AddRotateXYZOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(0, 45, 0))

# Set scale
xform.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0))

# Reset transforms
xform.ClearXformOpOrder()

## VariantSets

VariantSets provide switchable configurations:

```python
# Define variants
prim = stage.DefinePrim("/World/geo/chair", "Xform")
vset = prim.GetVariantSets().AddVariantSet("style")
vset.AddVariant("modern")
vset.AddVariant("classic")
vset.AddVariant("rustic")

# Set active variant
vset.SetVariantSelection("modern")

# Author inside variant
with vset.GetVariantEditContext():
    # Opinions here only apply when "modern" is selected
    stage.DefinePrim("/World/geo/chair/mesh", "Mesh")
```

In Houdini: `Add Variant` LOP node creates VariantSets. `Set Variant` LOP switches selection.

## Instancing

### Point Instancer (many copies, GPU efficient)

```python
from pxr import UsdGeom

instancer = UsdGeom.PointInstancer.Define(stage, "/World/instances")
instancer.CreatePrototypesRel().SetTargets(["/World/prototypes/tree"])
instancer.CreatePositionsAttr().Set([Gf.Vec3f(0,0,0), Gf.Vec3f(5,0,3)])
instancer.CreateOrientationsAttr().Set([Gf.Quath(1,0,0,0), Gf.Quath(1,0,0,0)])
instancer.CreateScalesAttr().Set([Gf.Vec3f(1,1,1), Gf.Vec3f(0.8,0.8,0.8)])
instancer.CreateProtoIndicesAttr().Set([0, 0])
```

### Native Instancing (shared subtrees)

Mark a prim as instanceable to share its subtree:
```python
prim.SetInstanceable(True)
```

All references to the same asset with `instanceable=True` share GPU memory.

## Visibility and Purpose

```python
# Hide prim (still composed, just invisible)
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).MakeInvisible()

# Show prim
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).MakeVisible()

# Purpose: default, render, proxy, guide
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).GetPurposeAttr().Set("render")
```

| Purpose | Viewport | Render | Use Case |
|---------|----------|--------|----------|
| `default` | Yes | Yes | Normal geometry |
| `render` | No | Yes | Render-only detail (displacement, subdivision) |
| `proxy` | Yes | No | Viewport stand-in (low-poly) |
| `guide` | Optional | No | Construction guides, debug geo |

## Material Binding

```python
from pxr import UsdShade

# Bind material to prim
material = UsdShade.Material.Get(stage, "/materials/chrome")
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).Bind(material)

# Bind to GeomSubset (face-level assignment)
subset = UsdGeom.Subset.Define(stage, "/World/geo/hero/face_group")
subset.CreateIndicesAttr().Set([0, 1, 2, 3])
subset.CreateElementTypeAttr().Set("face")
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(subset.GetPrim()).Bind(material)

# Collection-based binding (pattern matching)
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).Bind(
    material,
    bindingName="chrome_bind",
    materialPurpose="full"
)
```

# USD Stage Composition and Layer Workflows

## Composition Arcs (LIVRPS)

USD resolves opinions via **LIVRPS** strength ordering (strongest first):

| Arc | Strength | Use Case | Example |
|-----|----------|----------|---------|
| **L**ocal opinions | 1 (strongest) | Direct attribute edits on a prim | `prim.GetAttribute("radius").Set(2.0)` |
| **I**nherits | 2 | Share properties across prim classes | `inherits = </class/hero>` |
| **V**ariantSets | 3 | Switchable options on a prim | `variantSet "color" = { "red" { ... } "blue" { ... } }` |
| **R**eferences | 4 | Bring in external assets | `references = @./assets/chair.usd@` |
| **P**ayloads | 5 | Deferred-load references (lazy) | `payload = @./heavy_geo.usd@` |
| **S**ublayers | 6 (weakest) | Stack layers in a stage | `subLayers = [@./anim.usd@, @./model.usd@]` |

**Key rule**: A stronger arc's opinion always wins. Local edits override everything.

## Layer Stacking Patterns

### Multi-Department Pipeline

Standard production layer order (top = strongest):

```
shot_final.usd          (sublayer - comp's final tweaks)
  shot_fx.usd           (sublayer - FX overrides)
    shot_lighting.usd   (sublayer - lighting department)
      shot_anim.usd     (sublayer - animation curves)
        shot_layout.usd (sublayer - layout positions)
          asset.usd     (reference - model/materials)
```

Each department only edits their layer. Opinions cascade: lighting can override layout positions, FX can override lighting visibility.

### In Houdini/Solaris

```
sublayer1 (LOP) -> sublayer2 (LOP) -> merge (LOP)
```

- **Sublayer**: Stacks opinions (weaker than existing). Use for department overrides.
- **Reference**: Brings in an asset under a prim path. Use for asset loading.
- **Graft**: Moves a prim subtree to a new location. Use for scene assembly.

### Reference vs Sublayer Decision

| Scenario | Use | Why |
|----------|-----|-----|
| Loading an asset (chair, tree, character) | Reference | Isolates asset under target prim, can instance |
| Adding department overrides (lighting, FX) | Sublayer | Stacks on existing stage, opinions merge |
| Combining multiple shots | Sublayer | Each shot layer contributes to final |
| Instancing same asset N times | Reference + instanceable | Single prototype, many instances |
| Deferred loading (huge assets) | Payload | Like reference but lazy-loaded |

## Prim Hierarchy Best Practices

### Standard Scene Structure

```
/World
  /cameras
    /render_cam
    /turntable_cam
  /lights
    /key_light
    /fill_light
    /rim_light
    /dome_light
  /geo
    /hero
    /props
      /chair
      /table
    /environment
      /ground
      /walls
  /materials
    /hero_mat
    /props_chrome
    /ground_concrete
```

### Naming Conventions

- Use **snake_case** for prim names (not camelCase)
- Group by function: `/cameras/`, `/lights/`, `/geo/`, `/materials/`
- Assets get their own scope: `/geo/hero/` not `/hero/`
- Materials live under `/materials/` or `/World/materials/`

## Common Prim Types

| Type | Category | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| `Xform` | Transform | Grouping node with transform |
| `Mesh` | Geometry | Polygonal mesh |
| `BasisCurves` | Geometry | Curves (hair, wires) |
| `Points` | Geometry | Point cloud |
| `Sphere`, `Cube`, `Cylinder`, `Cone`, `Capsule` | Geometry | Implicit shapes |
| `DomeLight` | Lighting | Environment/HDRI light |
| `DistantLight` | Lighting | Sun/directional |
| `RectLight` | Lighting | Area light (rectangular) |
| `DiskLight` | Lighting | Area light (disk) |
| `SphereLight` | Lighting | Point/sphere light |
| `CylinderLight` | Lighting | Tube/strip light |
| `Camera` | Camera | Render camera |
| `Material` | Shading | Material container |
| `Shader` | Shading | Individual shader node |
| `Scope` | Organization | Non-transformable group |
| `GeomSubset` | Geometry | Face set for material binding |
| `RenderProduct` | Rendering | Output file definition |
| `RenderVar` | Rendering | AOV definition |

## Transforms

### Transform Stack

USD uses an ordered stack of transform operations:

```
xformOp:translate    -> position
xformOp:rotateXYZ   -> rotation (Euler)
xformOp:scale        -> scale
```

The `xformOpOrder` attribute defines execution order (right-to-left):
```python
xformOpOrder = ["xformOp:translate", "xformOp:rotateXYZ", "xformOp:scale"]
# Applied as: Scale first, then Rotate, then Translate
```

### Common Transform Operations

```python
# Houdini Python (inside LOP context)
from pxr import UsdGeom, Gf

stage = hou.pwd().editableStage()
prim = stage.GetPrimAtPath("/World/geo/hero")
xform = UsdGeom.Xformable(prim)

# Set translate
xform.AddTranslateOp().Set(Gf.Vec3d(1.0, 2.0, 3.0))

# Set rotation (degrees)
xform.AddRotateXYZOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(0, 45, 0))

# Set scale
xform.AddScaleOp().Set(Gf.Vec3f(1.0, 1.0, 1.0))

# Reset transforms
xform.ClearXformOpOrder()
```

## VariantSets

VariantSets provide switchable configurations:

```python
# Define variants
prim = stage.DefinePrim("/World/geo/chair", "Xform")
vset = prim.GetVariantSets().AddVariantSet("style")
vset.AddVariant("modern")
vset.AddVariant("classic")
vset.AddVariant("rustic")

# Set active variant
vset.SetVariantSelection("modern")

# Author inside variant
with vset.GetVariantEditContext():
    # Opinions here only apply when "modern" is selected
    stage.DefinePrim("/World/geo/chair/mesh", "Mesh")
```

In Houdini: `Add Variant` LOP node creates VariantSets. `Set Variant` LOP switches selection.

## Instancing

### Point Instancer (many copies, GPU efficient)

```python
from pxr import UsdGeom

instancer = UsdGeom.PointInstancer.Define(stage, "/World/instances")
instancer.CreatePrototypesRel().SetTargets(["/World/prototypes/tree"])
instancer.CreatePositionsAttr().Set([Gf.Vec3f(0,0,0), Gf.Vec3f(5,0,3)])
instancer.CreateOrientationsAttr().Set([Gf.Quath(1,0,0,0), Gf.Quath(1,0,0,0)])
instancer.CreateScalesAttr().Set([Gf.Vec3f(1,1,1), Gf.Vec3f(0.8,0.8,0.8)])
instancer.CreateProtoIndicesAttr().Set([0, 0])
```

### Native Instancing (shared subtrees)

Mark a prim as instanceable to share its subtree:
```python
prim.SetInstanceable(True)
```

All references to the same asset with `instanceable=True` share GPU memory.

## Visibility and Purpose

```python
# Hide prim (still composed, just invisible)
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).MakeInvisible()

# Show prim
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).MakeVisible()

# Purpose: default, render, proxy, guide
UsdGeom.Imageable(prim).GetPurposeAttr().Set("render")
```

| Purpose | Viewport | Render | Use Case |
|---------|----------|--------|----------|
| `default` | Yes | Yes | Normal geometry |
| `render` | No | Yes | Render-only detail (displacement, subdivision) |
| `proxy` | Yes | No | Viewport stand-in (low-poly) |
| `guide` | Optional | No | Construction guides, debug geo |

## Material Binding

```python
from pxr import UsdShade

# Bind material to prim
material = UsdShade.Material.Get(stage, "/materials/chrome")
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).Bind(material)

# Bind to GeomSubset (face-level assignment)
subset = UsdGeom.Subset.Define(stage, "/World/geo/hero/face_group")
subset.CreateIndicesAttr().Set([0, 1, 2, 3])
subset.CreateElementTypeAttr().Set("face")
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(subset.GetPrim()).Bind(material)

# Collection-based binding (pattern matching)
UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).Bind(
    material,
    bindingName="chrome_bind",
    materialPurpose="full"
)
```

## Common USD Attributes

|-----------|------|------------|-------------|
| `xformOp:translate` | double3 | Any Xformable | Position |
| `xformOp:rotateXYZ` | float3 | Any Xformable | Euler rotation |

1→# VEX Data Types and Conversions
     2→
     3→## Type Hierarchy
     4→
     5→| Type | Size | Description | Literal Example |
     6→|------|------|-------------|-----------------|
     7→| `int` | 4 bytes | 32-bit integer | `42`, `-1`, `0xFF` |
     8→| `float` | 4 bytes | 32-bit float | `3.14`, `1e-5`, `.5` |
     9→| `vector2` | 8 bytes | 2 floats | `{0.5, 0.5}` |
    10→| `vector` | 12 bytes | 3 floats (xyz/rgb) | `{1, 2, 3}` |
    11→| `vector4` | 16 bytes | 4 floats (quaternion/rgba) | `{0, 0, 0, 1}` |
    12→| `matrix2` | 16 bytes | 2x2 matrix | `ident()` |
    13→| `matrix3` | 36 bytes | 3x3 matrix (rotation/scale) | `ident()` |
    14→| `matrix` | 64 bytes | 4x4 matrix (full transform) | `ident()` |
    15→| `string` | varies | UTF-8 string | `"hello"` |
    16→
    17→## Implicit Conversions
    18→
    19→VEX promotes types automatically: `int -> float -> vector2 -> vector -> vector4`
    20→
    21→```vex
    22→float f = 5;            // int to float: f = 5.0
    23→vector v = 2.0;         // float to vector: v = {2, 2, 2}
    24→vector v = set(1, 2, 3); // explicit construction
    25→```
    26→
    27→## Explicit Conversions
    28→
    29→```vex
    30→int i = int(3.7);            // truncate: 3
    31→float f = float(42);         // promote: 42.0
    32→float x = v.x;               // component: or v[0]
    33→vector v = set(x, y, z);     // construct
    34→
    35→// String conversions
    36→string s = itoa(42);         // "42"
    37→string s = sprintf("%g", 3.14); // "3.14"
    38→int i = atoi("42");
    39→float f = atof("3.14");
    40→```
    41→
    42→## Quaternion Operations
    43→
    44→Quaternions are `vector4` with (x, y, z, w) layout:
    45→
    46→```vex
    47→// Identity (no rotation)
    48→vector4 q = {0, 0, 0, 1};
    49→
    50→// From axis-angle
    51→vector4 q = quaternion(radians(90), {0, 1, 0});
    52→
    53→// From Euler angles
    54→vector4 q = eulertoquaternion(radians(rot), XFORM_XYZ);
    55→
    56→// From matrix3
    57→matrix3 m = lookat({0,0,0}, {0,0,1});
    58→vector4 q = quaternion(m);
    59→
    60→// Apply rotation
    61→vector rotated = qrotate(q, @P);
    62→
    63→// Combine rotations
    64→vector4 q_combined = qmultiply(q1, q2);
    65→
    66→// Interpolate (spherical)
    67→vector4 q_blend = slerp(q1, q2, chf("blend"));
    68→
    69→// Invert
    70→vector4 q_inv = qinvert(q);
    71→```
    72→
    73→## Matrix Operations
    74→
    75→```vex
    76→// Identity
    77→matrix m = ident();
    78→
    79→// Build from components
    80→matrix m = maketransform(XFORM_TRS, XFORM_XYZ, translate, rotate, scale);
    81→
    82→// Extract components
    83→vector t, r, s;
    84→cracktransform(XFORM_TRS, XFORM_XYZ, {0,0,0}, m, t, r, s);
    85→
    86→// Transform point (includes translation)
    87→vector world_pos = @P * m;
    88→
    89→// Transform direction (no translation)
    90→matrix3 m3 = matrix3(m);
    91→vector world_dir = @N * m3;
    92→
    93→// Invert
    94→matrix inv = invert(m);
    95→
    96→// Look-at rotation
    97→matrix3 rot = lookat(from_pos, to_pos);
    98→
    99→// Rotation between two vectors
   100→matrix3 rot = dihedral(vec_a, vec_b);
   101→```
   102→
   103→## See Also

1→# Hydra Render Delegates Reference
     2→
     3→## Architecture Overview
     4→
     5→```
     6→USD Stage
     7→  +-- UsdImagingDelegate (translates USD prims -> Hydra prims)
     8→       +-- HdRenderIndex (scene database)
     9→            +-- HdRenderDelegate (your renderer)
    10→                 +-- HdRenderPass (executes rendering)
    11→                 +-- HdRenderBuffer (stores output: color, depth, normal)
    12→                 +-- HdRprim / HdSprim / HdBprim (scene primitives)
    13→```
    14→
    15→## Core Classes
    16→
    17→### HdRendererPlugin (Entry Point)
    18→
    19→The plugin registry discovers your renderer via `plugInfo.json`. This class creates delegates.
    20→
    21→```cpp
    22→#include <pxr/imaging/hd/rendererPlugin.h>
    23→
    24→class MyRendererPlugin final : public HdRendererPlugin {
    25→public:
    26→    HdRenderDelegate* CreateRenderDelegate() override;
    27→    HdRenderDelegate* CreateRenderDelegate(
    28→        HdRenderSettingsMap const& settingsMap) override;
    29→    void DeleteRenderDelegate(HdRenderDelegate* delegate) override;
    30→    bool IsSupported(bool gpuEnabled = true) const override;
    31→};
    32→```
    33→
    34→**plugInfo.json registration:**
    35→```json
    36→{
    37→    "Plugins": [{
    38→        "Info": {
    39→            "Types": {
    40→                "MyRendererPlugin": {
    41→                    "bases": ["HdRendererPlugin"],
    42→                    "displayName": "My Renderer",
    43→                    "priority": 50
    44→                }
    45→            }
    46→        },
    47→        "LibraryPath": "lib/hdMyRenderer.dll",
    48→        "Name": "hdMyRenderer",
    49→        "ResourcePath": "resources",
    50→        "Root": ".",
    51→        "Type": "library"
    52→    }]
    53→}
    54→```
    55→
    56→| Field | Purpose |
    57→|-------|---------|
    58→| `bases` | Must be `["HdRendererPlugin"]` |
    59→| `displayName` | Shown in Houdini renderer dropdown |
    60→| `priority` | Higher = preferred when multiple delegates available |
    61→| `LibraryPath` | Relative path to compiled DLL/so |
    62→| `Type` | `"library"` for compiled delegates |
    63→
    64→### HdRenderDelegate (Renderer Core)
    65→
    66→```cpp
    67→#include <pxr/imaging/hd/renderDelegate.h>
    68→
    69→class MyRenderDelegate final : public HdRenderDelegate {
    70→public:
    71→    // Required overrides
    72→    HdRenderParam* GetRenderParam() const override;
    73→    const TfTokenVector& GetSupportedRprimTypes() const override;
    74→    const TfTokenVector& GetSupportedSprimTypes() const override;
    75→    const TfTokenVector& GetSupportedBprimTypes() const override;
    76→
    77→    HdResourceRegistrySharedPtr GetResourceRegistry() const override;
    78→
    79→    // Prim factories
    80→    HdRprim* CreateRprim(TfToken const& typeId,
    81→                         SdfPath const& rprimId) override;
    82→    HdSprim* CreateSprim(TfToken const& typeId,
    83→                         SdfPath const& sprimId) override;
    84→    HdBprim* CreateBprim(TfToken const& typeId,
    85→                         SdfPath const& bprimId) override;
    86→
    87→    // Render pass
    88→    HdRenderPassSharedPtr CreateRenderPass(
    89→        HdRenderIndex* index,
    90→        HdRprimCollection const& collection) override;
    91→
    92→    // Settings
    93→    HdRenderSettingDescriptorList GetRenderSettingDescriptors() const override;
    94→};
    95→```
    96→
    97→**Prim Types:**
    98→
    99→| Category | Class | Examples |
   100→|----------|-------|---------|
   101→| Rprim (renderable) | `HdRprim` | Mesh, BasisCurves, Points, Volume |
   102→| Sprim (state) | `HdSprim` | Camera, Light, Material, RenderSettings |
   103→| Bprim (buffer) | `HdBprim` | RenderBuffer, RenderOutput |
   104→
   105→**Supported prim tokens (typical):**
   106→```cpp
   107→const TfTokenVector& MyRenderDelegate::GetSupportedRprimTypes() const {
   108→    static TfTokenVector types = {
   109→        HdPrimTypeTokens->mesh,
   110→        HdPrimTypeTokens->basisCurves,
   111→        HdPrimTypeTokens->points,
   112→    };
   113→    return types;
   114→}
   115→```
   116→
   117→### HdRenderPass (Per-Frame Execution)
   118→
   119→```cpp
   120→#include <pxr/imaging/hd/renderPass.h>
   121→
   122→class MyRenderPass final : public HdRenderPass {
   123→protected:
   124→    void _Execute(HdRenderPassStateSharedPtr const& renderPassState,
   125→                  TfTokenVector const& renderTags) override;
   126→};
   127→```
   128→
   129→The `_Execute` method is called each frame. It reads scene data from the render index, invokes your renderer, and writes results to render buffers.
   130→
   131→**Typical _Execute flow:**
   132→1. Get camera from `renderPassState`
   133→2. Query dirty prims from render index
   134→3. Sync scene changes (transforms, visibility, materials)
   135→4. Render frame (your rendering logic)
   136→5. Write pixels to `HdRenderBuffer`
   137→
   138→### HdRenderBuffer (Output Storage)
   139→
   140→```cpp
   141→#include <pxr/imaging/hd/renderBuffer.h>
   142→
   143→class MyRenderBuffer final : public HdRenderBuffer {
   144→public:
   145→    bool Allocate(GfVec3i const& dimensions,
   146→                  HdFormat format,
   147→                  bool multiSampled) override;
   148→    void* Map() override;          // Get raw pixel pointer
   149→    void Unmap() override;
   150→    bool IsMapped() const override;
   151→    void Resolve() override;       // Finalize (e.g., denoise, tonemap)
   152→
   153→    unsigned int GetWidth() const override;
   154→    unsigned int GetHeight() const override;
   155→    unsigned int GetDepth() const override;
   156→    HdFormat GetFormat() const override;
   157→    bool IsMultiSampled() const override;
   158→};
   159→```
   160→
   161→**Common formats:**
   162→| HdFormat | Use |
   163→|----------|-----|
   164→| `HdFormatFloat32Vec4` | RGBA color (HDR) |
   165→| `HdFormatFloat32` | Depth |
   166→| `HdFormatFloat32Vec3` | Normal, position AOVs |
   167→| `HdFormatUNorm8Vec4` | LDR color (8-bit) |
   168→
   169→### HdRenderSettingDescriptorList (Custom Settings)
   170→
   171→Exposes settings in Houdini's Render Settings LOP:
   172→
   173→```cpp
   174→HdRenderSettingDescriptorList
   175→MyRenderDelegate::GetRenderSettingDescriptors() const {
   176→    return {
   177→        {"Steps", TfToken("carwash:steps"), VtValue(20)},
   178→        {"CFG Scale", TfToken("carwash:cfg"), VtValue(7.0f)},
   179→        {"Prompt", TfToken("carwash:prompt"),
   180→         VtValue(std::string("photorealistic"))},
   181→    };
   182→}
   183→```
   184→
   185→**For full UI integration**, use a USD API schema (`CarWashRenderSettingsAPI`) deployed as a resource plugin. See `usd-schema-registration.md`.
   186→
   187→## Houdini-Specific Patterns
   188→
   189→### Karma Reference (Houdini 21)
   190→
   191→Karma registers TWO plugins:
   192→```
   193→houdini/dso/usd_plugins/
   194→+-- hdKarma/
   195→|   +-- resources/plugInfo.json     <- HdRendererPlugin (delegate)
   196→+-- usdKarma/

   229→                    "alias": {"UsdSchemaBase": "KarmaRenderSettingsAPI"},
   230→                    "autoGenerated": true,

   232→                    "schemaKind": "singleApplyAPI"

   234→            }
   235→        },

   237→        "Name": "usdKarma",
   238→        "Type": "resource"

   240→}
   241→```
   242→
   243→### hdCarWash Pattern (AI Renderer)
   244→
   245→Same dual-plugin pattern:
   246→```
   247→dso/usd/
   248→+-- hdCarWash/resources/plugInfo.json   <- Delegate DLL
   249→+-- usdCarWash/resources/plugInfo.json  <- Schema + SchemasForRenderers
   250→```
   251→
   252→**SchemasForRenderers** (maps delegate -> schema for Render Settings tab):
   253→```json
   254→"SchemasForRenderers": {
   255→    "HdCarWash": ["CarWashRenderSettingsAPI"]
   256→}
   257→```
   258→
   259→Note: Karma in Houdini 21 does NOT use `SchemasForRenderers` (Houdini handles it internally). Third-party delegates may need it for auto-discovery.
   260→
   261→## Render Delegate Lifecycle
   262→
   263→```
   264→1. Houdini starts -> PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME scanned
   265→2. PlugRegistry discovers plugInfo.json with HdRendererPlugin base
   266→3. User selects renderer in Render Settings LOP dropdown
   267→4. HdRendererPlugin::CreateRenderDelegate() called
   268→5. Delegate creates RenderPass, RenderBuffers
   269→6. Per frame: _Execute() called on RenderPass
   270→7. RenderBuffer::Map() exposes pixels to Houdini viewport
   271→8. On renderer switch/close: DeleteRenderDelegate()
   272→```
   273→
   274→## Common Issues
   275→
   276→| Issue | Cause | Fix |
   277→|-------|-------|-----|
   278→| Renderer not in dropdown | plugInfo.json not discovered | Check PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME |
   279→| Settings tab missing | Schema not registered | Deploy usdSchema resource plugin |
   280→| Black viewport | RenderBuffer format mismatch | Match HdFormat to AOV expectations |
   281→| Crash on delegate create | DLL dependencies missing | Check DLL deps with `dumpbin /dependents` |
   282→| Delegate loads but no render | `_Execute` not called | Verify RenderPass creation, check prim collection |
   283→

# USD Schema Registration Reference

## Two Deployment Strategies

| Strategy | When to Use | Compiles C++? | Provides Accessors? |
|----------|-------------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Resource-only** | UI/settings schemas, display metadata | No | No (use generic `GetAttribute`) |
| **Compiled library** | Custom prim types, typed accessors, Python bindings | Yes | Yes (`Get*()` / `Set*()` methods) |

**Rule of thumb:** If you only need the schema to appear in Houdini's UI (Render Settings tab, property panel), resource-only is sufficient. If you need C++ accessor classes or Python `UsdMySchema` wrappers, compile.

## usdGenSchema (Code Generator)

### Input Schema File

```usda
#usda 1.0
(
    subLayers = [
        @usd/schema.usda@
    ]
)

over "GLOBAL" (
    customData = {
        string libraryName = "usdMyRenderer"
        string libraryPath = "."
        string libraryPrefix = "UsdMyRenderer"
    }
) {}

class "MyRenderSettingsAPI" (
    inherits = </APISchemaBase>
    customData = {
        string className = "MyRenderSettingsAPI"
        token apiSchemaType = "singleApply"
        token[] apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo = ["RenderSettings"]
    }
    doc = "Render settings for My Renderer."
) {
    int myrenderer:steps = 20 (
        displayGroup = "Quality"
        displayName = "Steps"
        doc = "Number of render steps."
    )
    float myrenderer:quality = 0.8 (
        displayGroup = "Quality"
        displayName = "Quality"
        doc = "Render quality (0-1)."
    )
    string myrenderer:prompt = "" (
        displayGroup = "AI"
        displayName = "Prompt"
        doc = "Text prompt for AI generation."
    )
}
```

### Key Schema Directives

| Directive | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `inherits` | `</APISchemaBase>` | Makes this an API schema (applied to prims) |
| `apiSchemaType` | `"singleApply"` | One instance per prim (not multi-apply) |
| `apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo` | `["RenderSettings"]` | Restricts to RenderSettings prims only |
| `displayGroup` | `"Quality"` | Groups attributes in Houdini UI tabs |
| `displayName` | `"Steps"` | Human-readable label in UI |
| `libraryName` | `"usdMyRenderer"` | Plugin name for registration |
| `libraryPrefix` | `"UsdMyRenderer"` | C++ class name prefix |

### Schema Types

| Type | Inherits From | Applied How | Use Case |
|------|---------------|-------------|----------|
| **IsA schema** | `</Typed>` | Prim type (`def MyPrim`) | Custom prim types (geometry, lights) |
| **Single-apply API** | `</APISchemaBase>` | `ApplyAPI()` | Settings, metadata (render settings) |
| **Multi-apply API** | `</APISchemaBase>` | `ApplyAPI(instanceName)` | Per-instance data (collections, AOVs) |

### Running usdGenSchema

```bash
# Houdini's bundled usdGenSchema (Windows)
"C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 21.0.512\bin\usdGenSchema.cmd" schema.usda outputDir

# What it generates:
outputDir/
+-- api.h                          # Export macros
+-- tokens.h / tokens.cpp          # TfToken definitions
+-- myRenderSettingsAPI.h / .cpp   # C++ accessor class
+-- wrapMyRenderSettingsAPI.cpp    # Python binding
+-- wrapTokens.cpp                 # Python token binding
+-- generatedSchema.usda           # Compiled schema (deploy this)
+-- generatedSchema.classes.txt    # Class list
+-- generatedSchema.module.h       # Module header
+-- plugInfo.json                  # Template (has @PLUG_INFO_*@ vars)
```

**Important:** The auto-generated `plugInfo.json` contains template variables (`@PLUG_INFO_LIBRARY_PATH@`, `@PLUG_INFO_ROOT@`). These are meant for CMake substitution during build. For resource-only deployment, write your own `plugInfo.json` instead.

## Resource-Only Deployment

No compilation needed. Deploy two files:

### generatedSchema.usda

Copy directly from usdGenSchema output. Contains the compiled schema with all attribute definitions, defaults, display metadata.

### plugInfo.json (hand-crafted)

```json
{
    "Plugins": [{
        "Info": {
            "Types": {
                "MyRenderSettingsAPI": {
                    "alias": {
                        "UsdSchemaBase": "MyRenderSettingsAPI"
                    },
                    "apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo": ["RenderSettings"],
                    "autoGenerated": true,
                    "bases": ["UsdAPISchemaBase"],
                    "schemaIdentifier": "MyRenderSettingsAPI",
                    "schemaKind": "singleApplyAPI"
                }
            },
            "SchemasForRenderers": {
                "HdMyRenderer": ["MyRenderSettingsAPI"]
            }
        },
        "LibraryPath": "",
        "Name": "usdMyRenderer",
        "ResourcePath": "resources",
        "Root": "..",
        "Type": "resource"
    }]
}
```

| Field | Value for Resource-Only |
|-------|------------------------|
| `LibraryPath` | `""` (empty -- no DLL) |
| `Type` | `"resource"` |
| `Root` | `".."` (parent of `resources/` dir) |
| `bases` | `["UsdAPISchemaBase"]` for API schemas |
| `schemaKind` | `"singleApplyAPI"` or `"multiApplyAPI"` |
| `SchemasForRenderers` | Maps delegate name -> schema list (for Render Settings tab) |

### Directory Layout

```
usdMyRenderer/
+-- resources/
    +-- generatedSchema.usda    <- Schema definition
    +-- plugInfo.json           <- Resource-only manifest
```

This directory goes under a path on `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME`. See `pxr-pluginpath.md`.

## Compiled Library Deployment

For full C++ accessor classes and Python bindings.

### CMakeLists.txt

```cmake
find_package(pxr REQUIRED)

# Schema library
add_library(usdMyRenderer SHARED
    myRenderSettingsAPI.cpp
    tokens.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(usdMyRenderer
    usd usdGeom usdShade tf sdf vt
)
target_include_directories(usdMyRenderer PUBLIC
    ${PXR_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
)

# Python wrapper (optional)
add_library(_usdMyRenderer SHARED
    wrapMyRenderSettingsAPI.cpp
    wrapTokens.cpp
    module.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(_usdMyRenderer
    usdMyRenderer boost_python
)
```

### plugInfo.json (compiled)

```json
{
    "Plugins": [{
        "Info": {
            "Types": {
                "MyRenderSettingsAPI": {
                    "alias": {"UsdSchemaBase": "MyRenderSettingsAPI"},
                    "bases": ["UsdAPISchemaBase"],
                    "schemaKind": "singleApplyAPI"
                }
            }
        },
        "LibraryPath": "lib/usdMyRenderer.dll",
        "Name": "usdMyRenderer",
        "ResourcePath": "resources",
        "Root": "..",
        "Type": "library"
    }]
}
```

## Applying Schemas (Python)

```python
from pxr import Usd, Sdf

stage = Usd.Stage.CreateInMemory()
rs = stage.DefinePrim("/Render/settings", "RenderSettings")

# Apply API schema
rs.ApplyAPI("MyRenderSettingsAPI")

# Check if applied
assert rs.HasAPI("MyRenderSettingsAPI")  # Houdini 21 style (string-based)

# Read attributes (generic, works without compiled accessors)
steps = rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:steps").Get()  # -> 20
quality = rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:quality").Get()  # -> 0.8

# Write attributes
rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:steps").Set(50)

# List all schema properties
defn = Usd.SchemaRegistry().FindAppliedAPIPrimDefinition("MyRenderSettingsAPI")
for prop_name in defn.GetPropertyNames():
    print(prop_name)  # myrenderer:steps, myrenderer:quality, etc.
```

## Display Metadata (Houdini UI)

Houdini reads `displayGroup` and `displayName` from the schema to build the Render Settings UI:

| Metadata | Effect in Houdini |
|----------|-------------------|
| `displayGroup = "Quality"` | Creates "Quality" tab/section in Render Settings |
| `displayName = "Steps"` | Label shown next to the parameter widget |
| `doc = "..."` | Tooltip on hover |
| Attribute type (`int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`) | Widget type (slider, checkbox, text field) |
| Default value | Pre-filled value in UI |

**displayGroup ordering:** Groups appear in the order they're first encountered in the schema file. Place your most important group's first attribute earliest in the schema.

## Karma Schema Pattern (Houdini 21)

```
usdKarma/resources/
+-- generatedSchema.usda     <- KarmaRenderSettingsAPI (100+ attributes)
+-- plugInfo.json            <- Type=resource, LibraryPath=""
```

Karma does NOT use `SchemasForRenderers` in Houdini 21 -- Houdini handles the mapping internally for its own renderers. Third-party delegates should include it.

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Schema not found by `FindAppliedAPIPrimDefinition` | plugInfo.json not on plugin path | Check PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME |
| `ApplyAPI` fails | `apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo` mismatch | Apply to correct prim type (e.g., RenderSettings) |
| Settings tab missing in Houdini | Schema registered but no `SchemasForRenderers` | Add mapping in plugInfo.json |
| Auto-generated plugInfo has `@PLUG_INFO_*@` | Template vars not substituted | Write manual plugInfo.json for resource deployment |
| Attributes have wrong defaults | generatedSchema.usda stale | Re-run usdGenSchema, redeploy |
| `displayGroup` not showing | Missing from generatedSchema.usda | Ensure source schema has displayGroup metadata |

---
*Source: Pixar USD schema framework + usdGenSchema. Verified against Houdini 21.0 usdKarma + usdCarWash patterns.*
*Cross-reference: hydra-delegates.md for delegate registration, pxr-pluginpath.md for plugin discovery.*

## Render Delegate Lifecycle

```
1. Houdini starts -> PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME scanned
2. PlugRegistry discovers plugInfo.json with HdRendererPlugin base
3. User selects renderer in Render Settings LOP dropdown
4. HdRendererPlugin::CreateRenderDelegate() called
5. Delegate creates RenderPass, RenderBuffers
6. Per frame: _Execute() called on RenderPass
7. RenderBuffer::Map() exposes pixels to Houdini viewport
8. On renderer switch/close: DeleteRenderDelegate()
```

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Renderer not in dropdown | plugInfo.json not discovered | Check PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME |
| Settings tab missing | Schema not registered | Deploy usdSchema resource plugin |
| Black viewport | RenderBuffer format mismatch | Match HdFormat to AOV expectations |
| Crash on delegate create | DLL dependencies missing | Check DLL deps with `dumpbin /dependents` |
| Delegate loads but no render | `_Execute` not called | Verify RenderPass creation, check prim collection |

# USD Schema Registration Reference

## Two Deployment Strategies

| Strategy | When to Use | Compiles C++? | Provides Accessors? |
|----------|-------------|---------------|---------------------|
| **Resource-only** | UI/settings schemas, display metadata | No | No (use generic `GetAttribute`) |
| **Compiled library** | Custom prim types, typed accessors, Python bindings | Yes | Yes (`Get*()` / `Set*()` methods) |

**Rule of thumb:** If you only need the schema to appear in Houdini's UI (Render Settings tab, property panel), resource-only is sufficient. If you need C++ accessor classes or Python `UsdMySchema` wrappers, compile.

## usdGenSchema (Code Generator)

### Input Schema File

```usda
#usda 1.0
(
    subLayers = [
        @usd/schema.usda@
    ]
)

over "GLOBAL" (
    customData = {
        string libraryName = "usdMyRenderer"
        string libraryPath = "."
        string libraryPrefix = "UsdMyRenderer"
    }
) {}

class "MyRenderSettingsAPI" (
    inherits = </APISchemaBase>
    customData = {
        string className = "MyRenderSettingsAPI"
        token apiSchemaType = "singleApply"
        token[] apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo = ["RenderSettings"]
    }
    doc = "Render settings for My Renderer."
) {
    int myrenderer:steps = 20 (
        displayGroup = "Quality"
        displayName = "Steps"
        doc = "Number of render steps."
    )
    float myrenderer:quality = 0.8 (
        displayGroup = "Quality"
        displayName = "Quality"
        doc = "Render quality (0-1)."
    )
    string myrenderer:prompt = "" (
        displayGroup = "AI"
        displayName = "Prompt"
        doc = "Text prompt for AI generation."
    )
}
```

### Key Schema Directives

| Directive | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `inherits` | `</APISchemaBase>` | Makes this an API schema (applied to prims) |
| `apiSchemaType` | `"singleApply"` | One instance per prim (not multi-apply) |
| `apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo` | `["RenderSettings"]` | Restricts to RenderSettings prims only |
| `displayGroup` | `"Quality"` | Groups attributes in Houdini UI tabs |
| `displayName` | `"Steps"` | Human-readable label in UI |
| `libraryName` | `"usdMyRenderer"` | Plugin name for registration |
| `libraryPrefix` | `"UsdMyRenderer"` | C++ class name prefix |

### Schema Types

| Type | Inherits From | Applied How | Use Case |
|------|---------------|-------------|----------|
| **IsA schema** | `</Typed>` | Prim type (`def MyPrim`) | Custom prim types (geometry, lights) |
| **Single-apply API** | `</APISchemaBase>` | `ApplyAPI()` | Settings, metadata (render settings) |
| **Multi-apply API** | `</APISchemaBase>` | `ApplyAPI(instanceName)` | Per-instance data (collections, AOVs) |

### Running usdGenSchema

```bash
# Houdini's bundled usdGenSchema (Windows)
"C:\Program Files\Side Effects Software\Houdini 21.0.512\bin\usdGenSchema.cmd" schema.usda outputDir

# What it generates:
outputDir/
+-- api.h                          # Export macros
+-- tokens.h / tokens.cpp          # TfToken definitions
+-- myRenderSettingsAPI.h / .cpp   # C++ accessor class
+-- wrapMyRenderSettingsAPI.cpp    # Python binding
+-- wrapTokens.cpp                 # Python token binding
+-- generatedSchema.usda           # Compiled schema (deploy this)
+-- generatedSchema.classes.txt    # Class list
+-- generatedSchema.module.h       # Module header
+-- plugInfo.json                  # Template (has @PLUG_INFO_*@ vars)
```

**Important:** The auto-generated `plugInfo.json` contains template variables (`@PLUG_INFO_LIBRARY_PATH@`, `@PLUG_INFO_ROOT@`). These are meant for CMake substitution during build. For resource-only deployment, write your own `plugInfo.json` instead.

## Resource-Only Deployment

No compilation needed. Deploy two files:

### generatedSchema.usda

Copy directly from usdGenSchema output. Contains the compiled schema with all attribute definitions, defaults, display metadata.

### plugInfo.json (hand-crafted)

```json
{
    "Plugins": [{
        "Info": {
            "Types": {
                "MyRenderSettingsAPI": {
                    "alias": {
                        "UsdSchemaBase": "MyRenderSettingsAPI"
                    },
                    "apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo": ["RenderSettings"],
                    "autoGenerated": true,
                    "bases": ["UsdAPISchemaBase"],
                    "schemaIdentifier": "MyRenderSettingsAPI",
                    "schemaKind": "singleApplyAPI"
                }
            },
            "SchemasForRenderers": {
                "HdMyRenderer": ["MyRenderSettingsAPI"]
            }
        },
        "LibraryPath": "",
        "Name": "usdMyRenderer",
        "ResourcePath": "resources",
        "Root": "..",
        "Type": "resource"
    }]
}
```

| Field | Value for Resource-Only |
|-------|------------------------|
| `LibraryPath` | `""` (empty -- no DLL) |
| `Type` | `"resource"` |
| `Root` | `".."` (parent of `resources/` dir) |
| `bases` | `["UsdAPISchemaBase"]` for API schemas |
| `schemaKind` | `"singleApplyAPI"` or `"multiApplyAPI"` |
| `SchemasForRenderers` | Maps delegate name -> schema list (for Render Settings tab) |

### Directory Layout

```
usdMyRenderer/
+-- resources/
    +-- generatedSchema.usda    <- Schema definition
    +-- plugInfo.json           <- Resource-only manifest
```

This directory goes under a path on `PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME`. See `pxr-pluginpath.md`.

## Compiled Library Deployment

For full C++ accessor classes and Python bindings.

### CMakeLists.txt

```cmake
find_package(pxr REQUIRED)

# Schema library
add_library(usdMyRenderer SHARED
    myRenderSettingsAPI.cpp
    tokens.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(usdMyRenderer
    usd usdGeom usdShade tf sdf vt
)
target_include_directories(usdMyRenderer PUBLIC
    ${PXR_INCLUDE_DIRS}
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
)

# Python wrapper (optional)
add_library(_usdMyRenderer SHARED
    wrapMyRenderSettingsAPI.cpp
    wrapTokens.cpp
    module.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(_usdMyRenderer
    usdMyRenderer boost_python
)
```

### plugInfo.json (compiled)

```json
{
    "Plugins": [{
        "Info": {
            "Types": {
                "MyRenderSettingsAPI": {
                    "alias": {"UsdSchemaBase": "MyRenderSettingsAPI"},
                    "bases": ["UsdAPISchemaBase"],
                    "schemaKind": "singleApplyAPI"
                }
            }
        },
        "LibraryPath": "lib/usdMyRenderer.dll",
        "Name": "usdMyRenderer",
        "ResourcePath": "resources",
        "Root": "..",
        "Type": "library"
    }]
}
```

## Applying Schemas (Python)

```python
from pxr import Usd, Sdf

stage = Usd.Stage.CreateInMemory()
rs = stage.DefinePrim("/Render/settings", "RenderSettings")

# Apply API schema
rs.ApplyAPI("MyRenderSettingsAPI")

# Check if applied
assert rs.HasAPI("MyRenderSettingsAPI")  # Houdini 21 style (string-based)

# Read attributes (generic, works without compiled accessors)
steps = rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:steps").Get()  # -> 20
quality = rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:quality").Get()  # -> 0.8

# Write attributes
rs.GetAttribute("myrenderer:steps").Set(50)

# List all schema properties
defn = Usd.SchemaRegistry().FindAppliedAPIPrimDefinition("MyRenderSettingsAPI")
for prop_name in defn.GetPropertyNames():
    print(prop_name)  # myrenderer:steps, myrenderer:quality, etc.
```

## Display Metadata (Houdini UI)

Houdini reads `displayGroup` and `displayName` from the schema to build the Render Settings UI:

| Metadata | Effect in Houdini |
|----------|-------------------|
| `displayGroup = "Quality"` | Creates "Quality" tab/section in Render Settings |
| `displayName = "Steps"` | Label shown next to the parameter widget |
| `doc = "..."` | Tooltip on hover |
| Attribute type (`int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`) | Widget type (slider, checkbox, text field) |
| Default value | Pre-filled value in UI |

**displayGroup ordering:** Groups appear in the order they're first encountered in the schema file. Place your most important group's first attribute earliest in the schema.

## Karma Schema Pattern (Houdini 21)

```
usdKarma/resources/
+-- generatedSchema.usda     <- KarmaRenderSettingsAPI (100+ attributes)
+-- plugInfo.json            <- Type=resource, LibraryPath=""
```

Karma does NOT use `SchemasForRenderers` in Houdini 21 -- Houdini handles the mapping internally for its own renderers. Third-party delegates should include it.

## Common Issues

| Issue | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| Schema not found by `FindAppliedAPIPrimDefinition` | plugInfo.json not on plugin path | Check PXR_PLUGINPATH_NAME |
| `ApplyAPI` fails | `apiSchemaCanOnlyApplyTo` mismatch | Apply to correct prim type (e.g., RenderSettings) |
| Settings tab missing in Houdini | Schema registered but no `SchemasForRenderers` | Add mapping in plugInfo.json |
| Auto-generated plugInfo has `@PLUG_INFO_*@` | Template vars not substituted | Write manual plugInfo.json for resource deployment |
| Attributes have wrong defaults | generatedSchema.usda stale | Re-run usdGenSchema, redeploy |
| `displayGroup` not showing | Missing from generatedSchema.usda | Ensure source schema has displayGroup metadata |

---
*Source: Pixar USD schema framework + usdGenSchema. Verified against Houdini 21.0 usdKarma + usdCarWash patterns.*
*Cross-reference: hydra-delegates.md for delegate registration, pxr-pluginpath.md for plugin discovery.*
